compound.name: 1,8-cineole (eucalyptol)
compound.one_liner: The eucalyptus-camphor note shared by rosemary, sage and peppermint oils; tested as an isolated compound in asthma.

pharmacology.mechanism: An RCT reported a steroid-sparing effect in asthma, interpreted by the authors as anti-inflammatory [41]; the target was not defined in the abstract read.

evidence.claim: Isolated 1,8-cineole allowed more steroid-dependent asthma patients to reduce oral prednisolone than placebo.
evidence.outcome_summary: 12/16 on cineole vs 4/16 on placebo reduced oral steroids (p = 0.012); one small RCT.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

compound.teaching_note: Rosemary is a chemotype lesson: cineole reaches 38-55 % only in the Moroccan/Tunisian type, while in the Spanish type α-pinene equals or exceeds it [12].
gaps: Cineole safety (e.g. in infants) not researched.
